competences: The learner identifies key facts about organs of government part b.
The learner explains information about The legislature, executive and judiciary using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes legislature, executive, judiciary.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about organs of government part b.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about The legislature, executive and judiciary.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about organs of government part b.
materials: Chart showing organs of government part b
Primary Five SST reference on The legislature, executive and judiciary
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces organs of government part b. They ask "State one function of the executive arm of government." and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.content: It implements laws. Groups of people that make up the executive organ To provide social services People who belongs to the Executive Legislature is the national assembly of a country. Legislature is the law-making body in Uganda. Before Uganda became independent, the assembly was called the legislature council It is headed by the parliamentary speaker. People who belongs to the legislature To give advice to the executive To protect the national constitution Legislature is headed by the speaker of parliament. Important personalities in parliament.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about organs of government part b on the chalkboard, including "It implements laws. Groups of people that make up the executive organ; To provide social services People who belongs to the Executive". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: State one function of the executive arm of government. | Who heads the executive arm of the government? | Name the first executive prime minister of Uganda. | State any three duties performed by the executive organ of the government. | State tany three ways the legislature in a democratic government.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "State one function of the executive arm of government." and "Who heads the executive arm of the government?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on organs of government part b, asks "State one function of the executive arm of government." and follows up with "Who heads the executive arm of the government?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "State one function of the executive arm of government." and "Who heads the executive arm of the government?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "When did Uganda get her independence?"
